description: A diagnostic adapter for Self-EvolveRec that preserves a stable DiagnosisProbe interface while allowing the underlying recommender architecture to evolve. It uses observable training data and model behavior to diagnose recommendations across four Amazon categories.
motivation: Keep diagnosis compatible with architecture changes, prevent unsupported claims about users or products, and compare trials consistently using macro-average validation HR@10.
implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Access the trained module through view.model and adapt the SASRec compatibility methods when changing architectures. Batches contain (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B×L tensors. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps; unavailable review, rating, product-attribute, and simulator-trait signals must remain unobserved. Generate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for twenty real training users, five per category. Preserve all four dataset routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the pinned host evaluator. Validation selection uses macro HR@10 with 200 users per category and 99 unique negatives; test information remains unavailable.

originality.positive: Combines a stable diagnostic interface with explicit observability constraints and architecture adaptation.
originality.negative: The description specifies an integration contract rather than a new recommendation algorithm or diagnostic method.

future_potential.positive: Could support comparable, evidence-based diagnosis across evolving recommender architectures.
future_potential.negative: Its practical value depends on concrete probe definitions and whether diagnostic findings improve validation performance within the search budget.
